name: Log receipt photos to Google Sheets with German VAT rules, OpenAI Vision and Telegram

parameters.content:
## Log receipt photos to Google Sheets with German VAT rules, OpenAI Vision and Telegram

### How it works

1. You photograph a receipt and send it to a Telegram bot, which only answers chat ids listed in Config.
2. OpenAI Vision reads the merchant, date, gross, net, VAT, currency, line items and any separate tip.
3. A second model call picks the cost centre and decides the one question the maths depends on: whether German VAT is recoverable.
4. The deductible amounts are calculated in code, because a business meal, a foreign receipt and a blocked activity each use a different base.
5. A likely duplicate is flagged for your decision rather than written twice or silently dropped.
6. The row is appended to Google Sheets and confirmed in Telegram, and a voice note reply re-classifies that row in place.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Create a Telegram bot with @BotFather and add a Telegram credential.
- [ ] Put your Telegram chat id into `owner_chat_ids` in Config. It is empty by default and an empty list denies everyone, because this workflow writes to a real bookkeeping sheet.
- [ ] Add an OpenAI credential, used for the Vision read, the classification and the voice transcription.
- [ ] Add a Google Sheets credential and create the `Ausgaben` tab with every column listed in the Customization section, in that order, before the first run.
- [ ] Add a Google Drive credential and pick the folder that should hold the receipt images.
- [ ] Paste your spreadsheet URL into `sheet_url` in Config so the View Sheet buttons open the right document.

### Customization

The `Ausgaben` tab needs these columns in this order: Tracking ID, Date, Merchant Name, Gross, Net, VAT, Currency, Cost Center, Deductibility, Deductible Amount, Attendees, Tax Notes, Confidence, Needs Review, VAT Country, Deduction Base, Recoverable VAT, Needs FX, Tip Amount, VAT Deductible, Net Deductible, Net Non-Deductible, Total Deductible Expense. Create them all up front, because the Sheets node caches column positions at setup time.

The classification rules are written for Germany (§4 Abs. 5 EStG and §15 UStG). For another country, change `home_vat_country` in Config and adapt the rules in the two payload-building nodes, since the percentages and the blocked-activity category are country specific.

## Receive the Telegram update
A photo, a voice note or a button tap. The owner gate rejects any chat id that is not in Config.

## Start a new receipt
Acknowledges the photo and downloads it from Telegram.

## Read the receipt image
OpenAI Vision extracts merchant, date, gross, net, VAT, currency, line items and any tip.

## Report an unreadable photo
Says so instead of guessing at the numbers.

## Archive the image in Drive
Keeps the original photo as the audit trail for the row.

## Classify and price the expense
One model call picks the cost centre and decides whether German VAT is recoverable. The arithmetic runs in code.

## Check for a duplicate
Same normalised merchant, same gross, within three days.

## Warn about the duplicate
Nothing is written. You choose Add anyway or Ignore.

## Append the row and confirm
Writes to the sheet and confirms with buttons.

## Ask for a photo first
A plain text message has no receipt attached to work on.

## Handle a voice reply
A voice note only means something when it replies to a logged row.

## Transcribe the correction
Downloads the audio and transcribes it with OpenAI.

## Re-classify the stored row
Finds the row by its tracking id and re-runs the classifier with your added context.

## Update the row and confirm
Writes the corrected figures back in place.

## Handle a button tap
Routes the callback to add context, skip, delete or ignore.

## Ask for more context
Sends a reply prompt so a voice note can be attached to this row.

## Skip this receipt
Marks the card as skipped and leaves the sheet alone.

## Delete the logged row
Resolves the row by tracking id, deletes it and edits the card.

## Ignore the duplicate warning
Drops the stashed row and leaves the sheet unchanged.

// Build classification request with caption (if any) as context.

const j = $('Build Filename').item.json;
const driveResult = $('Upload Receipt to Drive').first().json;
const imageUrl = `https://drive.google.com/file/d/${driveResult.id}/view`;

const vision = j.vision || {};
const caption = j.caption || '';

const classifyPrompt = `You are a German tax expense classifier for a marketing agency in Berlin (paid ads, marketing automation, n8n workflows).

Classify into ONE of these cost centers (use exactly these names):
1. "Versicherungen & Gebühren", insurance, statutory fees, IHK
2. "Reisekosten", flights, trains, taxis, fuel, hotels, Airbnb
3. "Kommunikation & IT", phone, internet, software, SaaS, hosting, domains
4. "Bewirtungskosten", meals with clients/prospects (70% deductible, REQUIRES attendees + business purpose)
5. "Büro & Infrastruktur", office rent, coworking, hardware, furniture, supplies
6. "Marketing & Werbung", ad spend, creative assets, stock media
7. "Verwaltung", banking fees, payment processor fees, postal/shipping
8. "Beratung & Coaching", lawyers, tax advisors, coaches, courses, conferences, books
9. "(Digitale) Produktentwicklung", outsourced developers, designers, freelancers
10. "Sonstiges", only when nothing else fits\n\nDEFAULT BIAS: the user uploads a receipt because he believes it is a real business expense. Your default assumption should be that it IS deductible somehow, in some cost center, at some percentage. The 0% activity block is a narrow, specific exception (golf, yacht, spa, tickets, similar leisure activities), not a fallback for "I am not fully sure." When genuinely unsure between a normal cost center and the 0% activity block, and the receipt shows food or drinks anywhere in the line items, default to Bewirtungskosten 70%, not the 0% block. The 0% block should be rare, not routine.

CRITICAL, BEWIRTUNGSKOSTEN IS FOOD/DRINKS ONLY:

"Bewirtungskosten" is strictly food and beverages consumed by clients/prospects (restaurant meals, catering, drinks). NEVER classify activities as Bewirtungskosten.

ACTIVITY/ENTERTAINMENT EXPENSES (§4 Abs. 5 Nr. 4 EStG), 0% deductible, 0% VAT recoverable:
- Water activities: jet ski, boat rental, yacht, sailing, scuba, surfing
- Sports: golf, tennis, ski lift, mountain bike rental, fitness, climbing
- Hunting, fishing (explicitly named in the law)
- Theater, opera, concerts, sports events (tickets with clients)
- Spa, wellness, massage with clients
- Any "Erlebnis" / experience-style activity

These are "ähnliche Zwecke" per §4 Abs. 5 Nr. 4 EStG. BFH-Urteil VIII R 26/14: even when purely to entertain business partners, NOT deductible. VAT also non-recoverable (§15 Abs. 1a UStG).

When you detect this pattern:
- costCenter: "Nicht abzugsfaehig (Aktivitaet)" -- use this label, NEVER "Sonstiges", so it is visually distinct from a normal 100%-deductible miscellaneous expense. You should be able to tell at a glance which bucket a receipt landed in without reading the tax notes.
- deductibility: 0
- needsReview: true
- taxNotes: "Aufwendung für ähnliche Zwecke nach §4 Abs. 5 Nr. 4 EStG (Unterhaltung/sportliche Betätigung mit Geschäftsfreunden). Steuerlich NICHT abzugsfähig: 0% Betriebsausgaben, 0% Vorsteuerabzug. BFH-Urteil VIII R 26/14: auch bei rein geschäftlichem Anlass nicht absetzbar."

VENUE REPUTATION IS NOT EVIDENCE. Do not classify as an activity because the venue is a private members' club, a hotel, a rooftop bar, or has a fashionable/expensive reputation (e.g. Soho House, hotel bars, members' clubs). Those venues sell food and drinks like any restaurant, and a receipt for dinner or drinks there is Bewirtungskosten even if the same building also contains a gym, spa, pool, or cinema. Classify by what is ACTUALLY on the receipt (line items, description of what was consumed), never by the venue's brand, prestige, or amenities you happen to know about.

CONVERSATION TOPIC IS NOT EVIDENCE EITHER. Do not classify a meal as a non-deductible activity because of what was discussed, e.g. AI, cryptocurrency, marketing strategy, coaching, career advice, someone's business or Selbstaendigkeit, a client's Shopify store. None of that matters for classification. Sec 4 Abs.5 Nr.4 EStG is about the TYPE OF ACTIVITY the receipt actually paid for (golf, boat/yacht rental, spa treatment, event ticket, hunting/fishing), never about the substance of the conversation over food. A dinner, lunch, or drinks receipt from a restaurant, bar, cafe, or caterer is Bewirtungskosten at 70% deductible regardless of how technical, deep, or unrelated-to-core-marketing-work the conversation sounds in the user's own description. "We discussed AI strategies" or "we talked about crypto" describes WHY the meal was a business meal, it does not turn the meal into an activity. Only reclassify to the 0% activity block when the RECEIPT ITSELF is for one of the named non-eating activities.

VENUE NAMES to watch for: "Watersports", "Wassersport", "Golf Club", "Tennis", "Yacht", "Boats", "Charter", "Ski", "Spa", "Wellness", "Adventure", "Erlebnis", "Eventarena", venue name followed by any sport name, WHEN the receipt line items themselves are for that activity (green fees, lift pass, spa treatment, boat rental, class or lesson, entry ticket). A restaurant, bar, or members' club billing food and drinks is never on this list no matter its name.

If the receipt could be food OR activity (genuinely ambiguous from the line items themselves, not from the venue name): classify conservatively as activity (0% deductible), set needsReview=true, and note "Activity venue suspected, verify if food/drinks were the actual expense via Add Context." Do NOT apply this ambiguous-default just because the venue sounds upscale or membership-based; only apply it when the line items themselves do not clearly show food, drinks, or a meal.

NEVER fabricate food/drinks in tax notes when the receipt actually shows an activity. Be honest about what the receipt says.

germanTaxCategory mapping:
- Versicherungen & Gebühren -> "Versicherungen / Beiträge"
- Reisekosten -> "Reisekosten"
- Kommunikation & IT -> "Telefon, Internet & Software"
- Bewirtungskosten -> "Bewirtungskosten"
- Büro & Infrastruktur -> "Raumkosten / Bürobedarf / GWG"
- Marketing & Werbung -> "Werbekosten"
- Verwaltung -> "Verwaltungskosten / Nebenkosten Geldverkehr"
- Beratung & Coaching -> "Rechts- und Beratungskosten / Fortbildung"
- (Digitale) Produktentwicklung -> "Fremdleistungen"
- Sonstiges -> "Sonstige Betriebsausgaben"

DEDUCTIBILITY: Bewirtungskosten -> 70 (needsReview=true if no attendees). Team meals (employees only) -> Sonstiges 100. Everything else -> 100.

EXTRA: TAX NOTES, Be detailed and actionable. The user is not a tax expert. Write Tax Notes in plain English explaining WHAT the situation is, WHY it matters, and HOW to fix it if anything is missing.

For EVERY classification, Tax Notes must include at least one note, even for clean receipts. For clean ones, briefly explain WHY it's deductible.

Examples of good notes:
- "Bewirtungskosten requires named attendees per §4 Abs.5 EStG. Without them, the 70% deduction may be rejected. Add attendees via Add Context, full names of clients/prospects present, plus business purpose."
- "Kleinbetragsrechnung (under €250). Simplified VAT rules apply, full VAT breakdown not required on receipt itself."
- "Großbetragsrechnung (over €250), requires full receipt with merchant address, VAT ID, line items, separate VAT amount/rate. Verify all present before year-end."
- "Currency not EUR, record exchange rate for receipt date (Bundesbank reference rate) when filing."
- "Trinkgeld enthalten, tip is part of Bewirtungskosten, deductible at 70%."
- "Standard Reisekosten, 100% deductible per §4 Abs.5 EStG. Keep travel context (purpose, dates, destinations) documented."
- "Software/SaaS, verify reverse-charge handling in USt-Voranmeldung if provider is EU but not DE."

Set needsReview=true when:
- Missing attendees on Bewirtungskosten
- Missing VAT details on Großbetragsrechnung
- Non-EUR currency without exchange rate context
- Provider VAT ID missing on invoice
- Classification confidence genuinely uncertain.

RECEIPT DATA:
${JSON.stringify(vision, null, 2)}

USER CONTEXT (caption, may be empty):
"${caption}"

BUSINESS PURPOSE, Generate a formal, German tax-compliant business purpose in proper Geschäftsdeutsch. The user runs a Berlin marketing agency (paid ads / Meta + Google Ads, marketing automation, n8n workflows, performance marketing). Translate any context the user provides into formal German business language matching these patterns:

- "Besprechung [der/zu/zur] [topic]"
- "Abstimmung zu [topic]"
- "Austausch zu [topic]"
- "Strategisches Gespräch zur [topic]"
- "Geschäftliches Follow-up nach [event]"
- "Kooperationsgespräch mit [partner type]"
- "Networking-Gespräch mit konkretem geschäftlichem Bezug"

Representative examples (use as style/topic inspiration, adapt to actual context):
- "Besprechung der Meta Ads Strategie mit [Kunde]"
- "Abstimmung zur Kampagnenstruktur und Budgetverteilung"
- "Erstgespräch zu einer möglichen Kundenbeziehung"
- "Geschäftliches Follow-up nach vorherigem Kundentermin"
- "Austausch zu Marketing-Automatisierung und Workflows"
- "Besprechung der Funnel-Strategie und Conversion-Optimierung"
- "Strategisches Gespräch zur Neukundengewinnung"
- "Abstimmung zu Tracking, Pixel und Conversion-Daten"
- "Kooperationsgespräch mit potenziellem Geschäftspartner"
- "Besprechung zur Digitalisierung von Geschäftsprozessen"
- "Austausch zu KI-gestützter Marketingoptimierung"
- "Besprechung eines Angebots und Leistungsumfangs"
- "Abstimmung zu Projektumfang, Zeitplan und Budget"
- "Review der bisherigen Kampagnenperformance"
- "Besprechung von Leadgenerierung und CPL-Zielen"
- "Abstimmung zu Reporting und Performance-Auswertung"
- "Austausch zu E-Commerce Wachstumsstrategien"
- "Besprechung möglicher Projektanfragen"
- "Networking-Gespräch mit konkretem geschäftlichem Bezug"
- "Abschlussgespräch zu Projektstatus und nächsten Schritten"

Rules:
- Always formal German (Geschäftsdeutsch), never casual English
- If user provides client/company names, incorporate them
- If context is vague ("lunch with team"), keep it vague but formal ("Teaminterne Abstimmung zu laufenden Projekten")
- If no context at all and it's clearly business-related (e.g. taxi to client meeting), generate a plausible generic one like "Kundentermin in Berlin"
- For non-Bewirtungs/non-meeting expenses (software, office supplies), Business Purpose can be the operational reason: "Werbeplattform für Kundenkampagnen", "Tool zur Marketingautomation"

Return JSON exactly:
{"costCenter":"","germanTaxCategory":"","description":"max 80 chars","businessPurpose":"","attendees":"","deductibility":100,"taxNotes":"","missingForTax":["array of what's still missing per German tax law"],"confidenceScore":"High/Medium/Low","needsReview":false,"merchantCountry":"","hasRecoverableGermanVAT":false,"vatBlocked":false}

For "missingForTax": list what's needed per Bewirtungskosten/Reisekosten/etc. rules. e.g. ["attendees", "business purpose"] for client meals without those details. Empty array if nothing missing.

── VAT TREATMENT (decide, do not calculate) ──────────────────────────────
Decide whether this receipt carries RECOVERABLE GERMAN input VAT (Vorsteuer), and whether
the category BLOCKS VAT entirely. Output three fields (below). Rules:

• hasRecoverableGermanVAT = true  ONLY IF the merchant is in Germany (merchantCountry "DE")
  AND German VAT is shown at 19% or 7%.
• hasRecoverableGermanVAT = false for ANY foreign merchant (VAT of another country, or no
  VAT shown), and whenever you are unsure the merchant is German.
• vatBlocked = true for §4 Abs.5 Nr.4 activities (golf, yacht/boat, spa/wellness, tickets
  to sporting/cultural events with business partners, "Erlebnis"/experience venues) AND
  for business gifts over €50 (§4 Abs.5 Nr.1). These block BOTH the deduction and the VAT.
• If the receipt is an EU business SERVICE billed without VAT (SaaS, ad platform, digital
  tool): hasRecoverableGermanVAT=false; add taxNote "Reverse-Charge nach §13b UStG - im
  UStVA selbst zu verrechnen (Vorsteuer und Umsatzsteuer heben sich auf)."; needsReview=true.

Reminder for the tax note (do NOT compute amounts, code does that):
• A GERMAN business meal is 70% income-tax deductible on the NET, but its VAT is 100%
  recoverable (§15 Abs.1a S.2 UStG) - the 70% cut never reduces the Vorsteuer.
• A FOREIGN meal is 70% of the GROSS (no recoverable German VAT).
• A §4 Abs.5 Nr.4 activity is 0% deductible AND 0% VAT (§15 Abs.1a S.1 UStG) - never
  classify an activity as Bewirtungskosten.

Add to the returned JSON object:
  "merchantCountry": "",              // echo/inferred ISO-2
  "hasRecoverableGermanVAT": false,   // boolean
  "vatBlocked": false                 // boolean
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
`;

const requestBody = {
  model: 'gpt-4o-mini',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: classifyPrompt }],
  max_completion_tokens: 1400,
  response_format: { type: 'json_object' }
};

return [{ json: { chatId: j.chatId, vision, caption, imageUrl, requestBody } }];

const existing = $input.first()?.json;
if (!existing || !existing['Tracking ID']) {
  throw new Error('Existing row not found for ' + trackingId);
}

const oldContext = existing['Additional Context'] || '';
const combinedContext = oldContext ? (oldContext + ' | ' + newContext) : newContext;

• If the receipt is an EU business SERVICE billed without VAT (SaaS, ad platform, digital

• A GERMAN business meal is 70% income-tax deductible on the NET, but its VAT is 100%
  recoverable (§15 Abs.1a S.2 UStG) - the 70% cut never reduces the Vorsteuer.
